aspects.says: Against a boxed target such as BinaryOperator<Integer>, Math::max resolves to max(int, int) after unboxing, so a null argument throws NullPointerException, and Math::abs as an IntUnaryOperator leaves Integer.MIN_VALUE negative.
basis: section:The Interface's Parameter Types Choose the Overload; the Value at Run Time Doesn't
aspects.reason: the overload is fixed by a declared type the starter would have to leave open; the quiz's formatter question checks the same compile-time choice

aspects.says: A method that declares a checked exception doesn't fit Function; it needs an interface that declares the exception, or a wrapping lambda.
basis: section:A Method That Throws a Checked Exception Doesn't Fit `Function`
aspects.reason: a compile error with no wrong version that runs; unit 3.2.2 practises the fix

aspects.says: A reference to a method with one declaration lets javac choose submit(Callable) over submit(Runnable) when the method returns a value, so get() returns that value.
basis: section:An Exact Reference Lets javac Pick `submit(Callable)`; Overloading the Method Makes the Call Ambiguous

aspects.says: A reference to a generic method in a chain without a target type needs explicit type arguments, such as Collections::<String>emptyList.
basis: section:A Generic Method Needs Type Arguments When Nothing Else Gives Them
aspects.reason: a compile-time inference failure: the wrong version does not compile, so no graded test can tell it apart

aspects.says: A reference to an overloaded method gives inference no types, so comparing(m).reversed() stops compiling when m gains an overload; passing reverseOrder() to comparing or giving type arguments fixes it.
basis: section:An Inexact Method Reference Leaves Inference Without the Types It Needs

aspects.says: The chosen overload decides what a null does: valueOf(Object) writes "null", valueOf(char[]) throws.
basis: section:The Interface's Parameter Types Choose the Overload; the Value at Run Time Doesn't

aspects.says: Overloading the referenced method makes submit(this::m) ambiguous in every caller; a cast or a lambda fixes the call site.
basis: section:An Exact Reference Lets javac Pick `submit(Callable)`; Overloading the Method Makes the Call Ambiguous

aspects.says: The functional interface's parameter types choose which overload a reference names, once, at compile time; the argument's run-time class plays no part, so String::valueOf as a Function<Object, String> writes [C@... for a char[].
basis: section:The Interface's Parameter Types Choose the Overload; the Value at Run Time Doesn't

aspects.says: An int[] is never spread into a T... or Object... parameter, since it is not an Object[].
basis: section:A Varargs Method Packs the Interface's Arguments, So an Array Becomes One Element

aspects.says: An unbound reference's first interface parameter may be any subtype of the class before ::, but not a supertype.
basis: section:The Interface's Parameter Types Choose the Overload; the Value at Run Time Doesn't
aspects.reason: a wrong version does not compile, so no plant can pass the main cases; unit 4.3.2 practises the supertype case

aspects.says: A varargs method used through a fixed-arity interface packs the interface's argument into a new array, so an Object[] passed as Object becomes one element.
basis: section:A Varargs Method Packs the Interface's Arguments, So an Array Becomes One Element
